correctness.rationale: For each rate, the positive exponential mass is strictly monotone in the end time. A scalar intermediate-value construction equalizes all n Gramian coordinates. Positive dual weights force adjacent weighted exponentials to cross at the strictly ordered switch times; pairwise crossings are convex combinations of the intermediate switches, yielding a unique upper envelope almost everywhere. The universal inequality min_i w_i <= sum p_i w_i <= integral max_i p_i exp(-2lambda_i s) = m proves global optimality; its strict second inequality gives uniqueness. The standard Gramian inverse minimum-energy law gives energy 1/m. Standalone numeric checks replay equalization and dual envelope; infinite assertion is analytical. A potential failure at coincident rates is excluded by strict separation.

value.rationale: The single-at-a-time actuator constraint is a natural scarce-control resource question and inverse-smallest-Gramian energy is the exact worst-case unit-target cost. The result completely classifies the global optimum for any dimension and distinct stable diagonal rates, avoiding exponential schedule search. It proves every optimal coordinate is used in one contiguous block, identifies its order (slow-first in forward time), finds all switches by one scalar root, and proves uniqueness. This is a meaningful model-specific structural classification beyond a cheap sign check, and supplies a precise benchmark for sparse-control scheduling heuristics. Limitations to ideal continuous diagonal dynamics are explicit.
